meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'movie, film' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я всегда смотрел фильмы про войну.
examples.trans: I always watched movies about the war.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'a little; nearly', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

расплакаться.gloss: to burst into tears, start crying

meanings.en: to burst into tears, start crying
meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'плакаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to burst into tears, start crying', paired with 'плакать'.

examples.text: Что ты расплакался, как маленькая девочка?
examples.trans: Why are you crying like a little girl?
The child fell and burst into loud tears.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'end' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'never', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.

examples.text: Я своему ребёнку никогда не вру.
examples.trans: I never lie to my child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

подумать.gloss: to think (for a while), to think it over

meanings.en: to think (for a while), to think it over
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (for a while), to think it over', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

уметь.gloss: to know how to, to be able to

meanings.en: to know how to, to be able to
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know how to, to be able to', paired with 'суметь'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cry, to weep', paired with 'заплакать'.

examples.text: Ладно, не плачь. Это Лёля. Нравится?
examples.trans: All right, don't cry. That's Lyolya. Do you like her?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'head chef, executive chef' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

examples.text: Шеф-повар решит, подходите ли вы ресторану.
examples.trans: The head chef will decide whether you suit the restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Common Russian noun meaning 'kids; guys' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тогда ребята с тобой поработают. До свидания, Аркадий Борисович.
examples.trans: Then the boys will have a little word with you. Goodbye, Arkady Borisovich.
Then the boys will have a little word with you.
Right, kids, go out of the room.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strong, sturdy, firm').

examples.text: Рука у тебя крепкая, как у деда.
examples.trans: Your grip is strong, just like your grandfather's.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

успеть.gloss: to make it, to be in time

meanings.en: to make it, to be in time
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to make it, to be in time', paired with 'успевать'.

examples.trans: We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

examples.text: Ты успела отправить видео?! Зачем ты это сделала?
examples.trans: You managed to send the video?! Why did you do that?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'метить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to notice, spot', paired with 'замечать'.

examples.trans: He did not notice the loss.

examples.text: Никто на кухне ничего не заметил.
examples.trans: Nobody in the kitchen noticed anything.
And what if someone notices me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.en: for a long time; long ago
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

examples.text: Вспомнил? Я давно тебя не интересую.
examples.trans: Now you remember? You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спрашивать'.

examples.text: А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Ask him where he put the computer lab.

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Really? Then ask him where he put the computer lab.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'звание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'name, title' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I wrote the name on a piece of paper.

examples.text: Я написал название на этой бумажке.
examples.trans: I wrote the name on this piece of paper.

examples.text: Ты просто изменил старые названия на новые!
examples.trans: You simply changed old names to new ones!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'colour' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.
